notes.frame: the game's: x, y on the ground, z up, metres; triangles anticlockwise seen from outside
notes.placement: per track, exported here (kart_track.TRACKS are the only tracks): draw each track's parts as they are, and each shape at each of its instances: [x, y, z, h, s, r, g, b] = turn the shape h degrees anticlockwise about z, scale it by s, move it to (x, y, z); multiply the colours of its parts marked tint by (r, g, b)
notes.colours: vertex colours and tints are screen colours (sRGB): make them linear (c ** 2.2) as a material's colour is; the drawn colour is material colour x vertex colour x tint x texture
notes.materials: texture sets are kart_gfx.py's (and the engine's steel, concrete) as make_textures.py writes them to tex/: <texture>_albedo (sRGB), _mr (red: occlusion, green: roughness, blue: metal; times the material's rough and metal), _normal; uvs are in repeats already
notes.decal: drawn over the road: a small depth offset (the window: Panda's setDepthOffset(1))
notes.two_sided: seen from behind too (no back-face culling)
notes.far: out in the country: no shadow (the window hides it from the sun's shadow camera)
notes.signs: the signs texture is one row per SIGNS entry, top first: CLUB CODERS, KART LAB, ROBOT LAB, FIGHT LAB, print("GO!"), BUILD  TEST  RACE, if fast: brake(), START
notes.lamp: the start lights: five pairs on the gantry, parts lamp 1 to lamp 5 (group 1 to 5) from the left as the grid sees them, dark red glass; "lights" says when each is lit (kart_scenery.start_lights: from "from" seconds before GO one more pair each "step" seconds, all out at GO) and their glow unlit and lit (linear light, as emission)
notes.water: the pond's texture coordinates are metres / its material's metres; "flows" says how they move (kart_scenery.water_offset): drift metres a second, plus sway times sin(2 pi t / sway_period), divided by metres
notes.group: a part drawn apart from the others of its material, because it changes while racing
notes.bridge: a footbridge over the road (kart_scenery.Circuit.bridge) is in the track's parts
notes.tv_cameras: kart_scenery.tv_cameras(track) = kart_gfx.ChaseCamera's six TV cameras: nothing taller than a barrier within 10 m of one
